question: Does Solivas-Tubaña's 2009 Abra freshwater profile expose species-level or dated, waterbody-resolved fish evidence for the CAR inventory?

source.citation: Solivas-Tubaña, C. (2009). Profiles of Endemic Freshwater Ecosystems in Abra. Journal of ISSAAS, 15(2), printed p. 191.
source.printedPageEvidence: The contribution begins on printed page 191 of the official Volume 15, Number 2 full-issue PDF; the following contribution begins on page 192.
source.publicationType: Short contribution in a journal issue. The reviewed page does not establish whether this is a full research article, conference abstract, or summary of a separate underlying report.
source.licenseFinding: No item-specific reuse license for this contribution or its underlying data was verified. Free access to the full issue is not treated as permission to reproduce its content.

scope.studyAreaAsPrinted: Abra Province; mentions the Abra River, tributaries, creeks, streams, and rice fields collectively.
scope.richnessInterpretation: The contribution claims 38 fish species but gives no complete checklist, taxon-by-site matrix, or counting method in the reviewed page. Do not treat 38 as a verified regional checklist or add it to other source totals.
scope.labelInterpretation: The first five are described as common labels and ludong is separately described as common in the province. The page supplies no scientific-name crosswalk, specimen evidence, or label-to-waterbody assignment; the six local labels are not assumed to represent six of the claimed 38 species.

limitations: No field date, sampling method, effort, named tributary or station, coordinates, vouchers, or identification authority is supplied on the reviewed page.
The broad Abra profile does not establish which river, creek, stream, rice field, or reach supports any individual label.

The relationship, if any, between this contribution and Segismundo and Felicitas (2009), the 2010 ISSAAS Abra abstracts, or the cited STARM material is unresolved; do not count them as independent surveys without source-lineage evidence.
The contribution's conservation and abundance wording is not treated as current status, present abundance, catchability, legal status, or safety evidence.
No item-specific reuse terms or underlying report/data package were found in this bounded review.

disposition.sourceUse: Research-only lead for tracing the claimed Abra freshwater profile and its underlying fish checklist or survey records.

nextAction: Seek the underlying survey report or a complete, attributable checklist from the author, Abra State University, or the journal archive; request field dates, waterbody/station crosswalk, identification basis, vouchers, relationship to the 2001/2010 Abra studies, and item-specific reuse terms. Until then, preserve only the source-reported aggregate and vernacular labels as unresolved research leads.

sources.supports: Official primary issue PDF; printed page 191 contains the Abra profile title, author/institution attribution, 38-fish claim, broad habitat context, and vernacular labels.
Official ISSAAS journal issue archive used to identify the journal's public issue archive; no item-specific reuse grant was identified.
